headline: Dry, sunny days with frosty mornings through Monday, possible midweek rain, and warmth by Friday.
summary: A low pressure system that brought showers to the region is pulling away to the southeast, and the last showers should end tonight. Behind it, drier high pressure is building in, bringing cool air from the northeast. That means clear, dry days and cold nights. Sunday and Monday mornings bring frost to many lowland and foothill areas, especially south of Seattle, while Monday afternoon warms to the upper 50s to mid 60s, near normal. Clouds return Tuesday as a weak stream of moisture aims mostly at British Columbia. Forecasters are unsure whether it will drift over western Washington midweek, and many computer model runs keep us dry. Warmer, drier weather returns Thursday, with highs in the lower 70s by Friday, though the weekend could bring rain and cooler air.
changes: The evening update largely repeated the afternoon forecast, and the midweek rain chance is still uncertain. The frost advisory areas for Sunday and Monday mornings were reworded but are essentially the same.
